plan: [Third-price auction with three bidders: the winner pays the lowest bid. Assume symmetric linear bids s(v)=c v; solving the best-response condition gives c=2, so the equilibrium strategy is b=2v. This maximizes expected long-run profit under independent uniform draws. With my private value $34, I should bid 2*34 = $68 (allowed in $0.1 increments).]

[Opponents' bids unknown; assume symmetric increasing strategies and, as a tractable benchmark, that they bid their values (uniform on [0,49]). If opponents' bids are iid U(0,49), my win probability = (b/49)^2 and conditional payment ≈ b/3, so expected profit proportional to b^2(28 - b/3), which is increasing up to b=56. Constraint b≤49 => optimal bid at the upper bound. Bid the maximum allowed (49) to maximize expected surplus.]

[Third-price (3rd of 3) means the winner pays the lowest of the three bids. If I bid b ≤ my value v=14, any win implies the lowest opponent bid < b ≤ v so payoff ≥0; increasing b up to v strictly raises win probability without risking negative profit. Bidding above v can cause losses if opponents both bid between v and my bid. So bid my true value: 14. ]
